candidates.buyer: Owner-operators and small firms running water or sewage tankers, who need a permit from the regional water utility
candidates.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers (also 13 and 18)
candidates.existing: The Arabic competitor search found no Oman platform for tanker operators. Licensees (the utility operating companies) must run the electronic register and install the tracking devices, so the likely software sits with the utilities and not the operators. A Saudi 'Tasreeh' platform from National Water Company is a different country.
candidates.name: Independent water and sewage tanker operator permit and SLA compliance kit
candidates.trigger: APSR Decision 31/2025 (Gazette 1593, 27 Apr 2025, effective the next day). No tanker may operate without a permit and a signed unified SLA (Art. 2-3). Existing operators had one year, to about late Apr 2026, to comply. Colour-coding and Arabic labelling (Art. 6). Tank cleaning and disinfection, inspection and complaint records (Art. 5(5), 7). Data supplied on request (Art. 7(5)). Fines OMR 50-5,000 for individuals and OMR 500-50,000 for companies, doubled on repeat, up to OMR 50 a day (Art. 8). Muscat Municipality sewage-vehicle rules of 29 Jun 2026 add a licence plate and approved disposal points.
candidates.unchecked: Operator count and whether permits are renewed each year (the text says nothing on validity); whether operators must file periodic reports or only respond on request; whether utilities already have a portal and tracker vendors for this; the exact start of the one-year deadline; whether fines are being enforced now that the deadline has passed.

candidates.buyer: Licensed recruitment offices, which sell to households
candidates.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies (also 1)
candidates.existing: None searched; the Arabic competitor search covered only the licensing rule.
candidates.name: Recruitment office compliance kit: e-registered domestic-worker contracts, no-fee rule and worker-file archive
candidates.trigger: The domestic-worker decision (reported as MD 475/2025 or 574/2025; effective Oct 2025) requires Arabic contracts registered on the MoL platform, bans recruitment fees charged to workers, and sets 3 months to regularise. Social Development MD 405/2025 created an association of recruitment offices.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed offices; whether the association mandates membership or reporting; actual office-level duties (licence renewal, bank guarantee, returns); competitors; whether offices (not households) are the payers. K04 targets households through offices, this targets the offices themselves, so the buyer differs.

candidates.buyer: Small operators who rent buses and drivers to schools (22,242 school buses in Oman)
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.existing: Not searched. Naql (MTCIT) platform is the state licensing system; the education ministry is working on technology for bus safety.
candidates.name: School-bus owner and contractor compliance (vehicle operating card, bus age, driver eligibility, renewals)
candidates.trigger: Ministry of Education regulation of rented school buses (2020): valid registration and vehicle operating card from MTCIT, bus age at most 12 years, driver Omani aged 23-60 with 5 years' experience; operators told to follow rules each new academic year (Oman Observer, Oct 2026).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the rules above are still current; contract and payment process with schools; tracker or tender-portal systems; competitor search not run (budget). Whether the buyer group is mostly Omani owner-drivers with a few vehicles.

candidates.buyer: Owner-operators of goods vehicles
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.existing: Tracker vendors exist in the Gulf generally (not searched in Oman); Naql is the state platform.
candidates.name: Goods-vehicle tracking and licence compliance for small trucking owners
candidates.trigger: Carriage by Land executive regulation amendments (MTCIT, 2023): tracking systems required for goods transport licensees; tampering fined, licence cancelled on the third offence. Naql platform for licences.
candidates.unchecked: Whether a reporting duty exists beyond installing the device; vendor coverage; likely already served by hardware tracker sellers.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: New domestic-worker decision (reported as MD 475/2025 or 574/2025, number conflicting; in force from about 9-13 Oct 2025): Arabic contracts registered electronically on MoL platform, no recruitment fees charged to workers, 12h/day cap, 21 days leave, records kept 1 year after service, 3-month transition, under-21 ban. Nothing new beyond K04 for households.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: 2022 activity-licence regulation (1-year licence, OMR 300 fee, 30-day renewal notice, 400 m2 site, concrete floor, governorate approves; issuing body not confirmed); Dhofar scrap order 2013; ban on scrap collection in residential areas with OMR 500 fine; Environment Authority 2021 waste-export rules. No register or report duty found. Weak.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Oman regime found for pawnbrokers or purchase registers on second-hand goods. Only used-car selling permit rules (Muscat Municipality 2018; Sohar order 2019 limiting to industrial areas, OMR 100 fine). Unverified.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05. Precious metals and stones AML supervision regulation exists (Gazette issue 1473, text garbled, date unconfirmed); Royal Decree 30/2016 is the AML law.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: NCSI figures via Oman Daily: about 1,527 vehicle-parts establishments to end Apr 2024, of which 671 retail used parts. No licensing, register or environmental take-back rule found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Only a camel digital ID / microchip plan (Oman Observer, undated) and Muscat Municipality abattoir hours. No mandatory trader register found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Municipal abattoirs (Muscat Municipality) serve individuals and meat shops; no private abattoir or butcher reporting duty found. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Only 2016 ministerial decisions (194/2016 ban on exporting Omani bee breeds, fine OMR 500-1000; 209/2016 hive movement ban, expired) and a subsidised hive programme. No beekeeper register or health certificate rule found. Tiny market. Weak.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Vet Practice Law RD 22/2017 with regulation MD 23/2021 (ministry register, licence renewal); Veterinary Preparations Law RD 34/2017 with regulation MD 60/2023 and fee decision MD 67/2023 (Gazette 1485, 19 Mar 2023). No record-keeping duty details seen; group is small. Weak/unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Wells and Aflaj regulation MD 264/2000 amended by MD 193/2023: contractors must register and are classified by capacity. About 6,660 water licences to end-2024, of which 3,990 well licences, 2,280 well registrations, 151 drilling-contractor applications. Small buyer group, ministry-run process.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: APSR Decision 31/2025 licensing independent water/wastewater tanker operators (see candidate C1). Muscat Municipality sewage-vehicle health rules published 29 Jun 2026. Be'ah holds the municipal waste monopoly; governorates taking over container collection from 1 Dec (year unconfirmed). No septage manifest found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Occupational safety regulation (2008, amended by MoL MD 4/2021): boilers tested every 12 months, steam and air receivers every 24 months by a competent person, with a register of test date, technician and remarks (Curtis blog 2016, current force unconfirmed). No Oman lift-inspection source found. Weak.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water and Wastewater Sector Regulation Law RD 40/2023 (6-month transition for regulated activities, extendable 6 months). Covered through the tanker candidate C1; no separate private small-system reporting duty found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pesticide Law RD 64/2006; regulation MD 41/2012; MD 160/2023 replaced the lists with List A (prohibited, holders must dispose within 6 months) and List B (restricted). The ministry issued 225 retail fertiliser sale licences and 96 pesticide registration certificates in one year (year unconfirmed); North Batinah ran 6,097 inspection visits. No mandatory sales register found. Weak.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Social Development MD 405/2025 (20 Nov 2025) created an association of recruitment offices; the new domestic-worker decision bans recruitment fees and requires e-registered contracts. Office licensing rules and office count not found. See candidate C2.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Interior Ministry cemetery regulation, Gazette 1544 (2024): municipality permits cemeteries and keeps the grave register; death report needed for burial. Municipal function, no private funeral-service licensing regime found. Not a software buyer.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Ministry of Social Development supervises 173 associations (68 Omani Women's Association branches, 42 charities, 40 professional, 23 expatriate community clubs; Oman Daily 2024). A Civil Society Institutions Law with exemptions was reported by Al Rai (date unconfirmed); annual audited accounts reviewed by the ministry under the 2001 law. Small, institutional buyers. Weak. No halal supervision body found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: 22,242 school buses (Oman Observer, 13 Sep 2026); rented school buses need a vehicle operating card, a maximum age of 12 years, and drivers aged 23-60 with 5 years' experience. Carriage by Land regulation amended 2023: tracking systems required for goods carriers; MTCIT Naql platform for licences. Taxis stay rejected (K13). See candidates C3 and C4.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money Services Business regulation published Apr 2024 (CBO) covers exchange houses, but they are few and licensed. Market traders and street vendors were not searched, so that part is not_reached.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Nurseries: 355 nurseries, 8,706 children (mid-2024); Social Development ministerial decision 48/2017 sets fees (OMR 100 a year individuals, OMR 200 companies); the minister was reported studying home nursery licensing (date unknown). Driving schools: Royal Oman Police 2024 regulation covers instruction offences (age 18, no night lessons 22:00-06:00). Tattoo studios, food producers and hunting outfitters not searched.

candidates.buyer: Owners of guest houses, rest houses, lodges, small hotels and classified restaurants/cafes; their accountants and PRO bureaus
candidates.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals (also 38)
candidates.existing: Competitor search (English, tourism fee + service charge + PMS) found no Oman-specific compliance product and no certified-software requirement; only the regulation commentary. Hotel PMS vendors presumably exist but were not seen. Oman Arab Bank has a digital service for tourism facilities (probably the fee payment channel).
candidates.name: C01 Tourism-regulation compliance kit for small tourist establishments (4% tourism fee, 8% service-charge distribution, annual declaration, 3-year classification renewals)
candidates.trigger: Ministerial Decision 1152/2/1/141/2026 (Executive Regulation of Tourism Law, RD 69/2023), in force 17 April 2026; 6-month transition ends about 17 Oct 2026. Quarterly 4% fee with auditor-certified statements, 8% service charge paid in cash to staff with a statement (circular effective 30 July 2026), annual declaration within 3 months and audited accounts within 2 months of year end, fines OMR 500-6,000, licence revoked after 5 months of unpaid fees.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed guest houses/lodges and their accountant practices; whether the Ministry has an online declaration portal that already does the 4% return; what the 'electronic link' with MHT/ROP requires; full regulation text; whether holiday homes are covered. Arabic competitor search not run (budget).

candidates.buyer: Licensed real estate brokerage offices and small developers (MoHUP-registered)

candidates.name: C02 AML/CFT compliance kit for real estate brokerage offices and small developers
candidates.trigger: MoHUP Ministerial Decision 244/2022 (Gazette 1473, 25 Dec 2022; replaces 113/2021): written risk assessment, customer due diligence including beneficial owner, written policies, internal audit, staff training, reports to the National Centre for Financial Information. Brokering without a licence is punishable by up to 6 months and OMR 3,000. A draft Real Estate Regulation Law (25 July 2026 news) is pending.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed brokers; whether inspections or fines are actually enforced; how the NCFI reporting channel works (goAML or similar); overlap with the draft Real Estate Regulation Law. Same duty type as K05 but a different buyer group.

candidates.trigger: Lease must be registered with the municipality; fixed 3% of annual rent; non-registration fined at 3x the fee; RD 12/2025 amended RD 6/89 and set up governorate rent-dispute committees (secondary source).

candidates.existing: Not searched in competitor form (budget). Payroll tools (Zoho, Keka, Odoo) cover Omanisation reporting inside payroll per K07; a standalone small-firm planner was not checked.
candidates.name: C04 Omanisation compliance planner for micro and small firms (one Omani per commercial registration, employment plan, SPF registration, permit-ban tracker)
candidates.trigger: Ministry of Labour 5 May 2025 statement and 15 June 2025 mechanism: every CR older than 1 year must employ at least one Omani registered with SPF; employment plan within 1 month of notice; 3 months (10+ staff) or 6 months (smaller) to comply; ban on new work permits if not. MD 602/2025: 30% permit-fee discount when meeting Omanisation targets, double fees otherwise. MOCIIP Decision 411/2025 for foreign-investor firms. MD 317/2025 sets a minimum annual increment for Omani private-sector staff (OMR 50 per employee penalty).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the Ministry portal already shows firms their status and plan; real pain for firms who cannot find an Omani (a hiring problem rather than a software one); who pays (PRO bureaus?); competitor search. Different duty from the rejected payroll idea K07 and from K03.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: MoH private health establishment licence renewal is on the e-health portal (renew from 1 month before expiry to 1 month after, then a penalty; centre OMR 450 Muscat / OMR 300 elsewhere). New fee structure announced and a 2024 decision (MD 231/2024) requires a bank guarantee. Insurer billing is Dhamani, already rejected as K10. Nothing new beyond K10 for billing. Renewal calendar only is weak (C09).

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacy executive regulations MD 113/2020 and fee schedule exist (pharmacy renewal OMR 300). No national track-and-trace mandate (K09). No 'precursor' list found, but Environment Authority Decision 50/2023 (hazardous chemicals) requires an environmental permit to import, sell, distribute or use, with semi-annual reports, a chemical database, SDS and Civil Defence storage/transport licences. See C05.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Security guard services need a royal-decree licence (RD 24/99, 25/99, with ROP approval). Labour-supply licence under the Labour Law. Cleaning establishments need MD 115/2020 conditions to bring in expat workers. Current licence categories and reporting are unverified. Related duties: Omanisation (C04), permit late fines (C11). Weak (C12).

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Tender Board Decision 104/2022 (classification and registration of contractors, suppliers, consultants); ICV principle (10% local value) in government tenders; JSRS registration for oil and gas suppliers; ICV certificate in energy was in a pilot with 2025 rollout (status unverified). Contractor classification and ICV reporting could be a niche but are not confirmed as recurring for small firms (C14, weak/unverified).

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Real estate brokers and developers: MoHUP Ministerial Decision 244/2022 (Gazette 1473, 25 Dec 2022), replacing 113/2021, imposes AML/CFT duties (customer due diligence, beneficial owner, written risk assessment, policies, internal audit, staff training, reporting to the National Centre for Financial Information). A draft Real Estate Regulation Law (Oman Daily, 25 July 2026) would unify brokerage, valuation, off-plan and escrow, status unknown. Lease registration at the municipality (3% fee, penalty three times the fee) and RD 12/2025 amendments are a landlord duty. See C02, C03.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Strongest finding. Tourism Law Executive Regulation, Ministerial Decision 1152/2/1/141/2026, in force 17 April 2026, repeals the previous regulations; existing licensees have 6 months (about 17 October 2026). Duties: 4% tourism fee remitted quarterly with auditor-certified statements; 8% service charge distributed to staff in cash with a statement to the Ministry (circular in force 30 July 2026); annual tourism fee declaration within 3 months of year end; audited accounts within 2 months; responsible manager; electronic link with the Ministry and ROP; 3-year classification certificate for restaurants/cafes. Hotels must also send guest and visitor data daily to ROP via an online portal (older rule). Fines OMR 500-6,000. Short-term rental licensing exists via MHT. See C01.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Fish exports need a Fish Quality Control Centre number, catch certificate (EU catch certificate via Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, free, 1-3 days), and lists of boat users attached to small-boat licences. No new mandate found; import side is covered by K01. Weak (C10).

coverage.category: 31. Omanisation: one Omani per commercial registration (MoL 2025)
coverage.found: Ministry of Labour requirement from 5 May 2025 (mechanism 15 June 2025): every commercial registration older than 1 year must employ at least one Omani registered with the SPF. Firms with zero Omanis must submit an employment plan within 1 month of notice; 10+ staff comply in 3 months, smaller firms 6 months; sole proprietors managing the business are exempt for 1 year. Non-compliance means a ban on new work permits. MOCIIP Decision 411/2025 covers foreign-investor firms. Oman Observer (July 2026) reports over 245,000 firms with zero Omani employees. MD 602/2025 gives a 30% permit-fee discount for meeting Omanisation and doubles fees for non-compliance. See C04.

coverage.category: 32. Expatriate work-permit renewal and late-registration fines (MD 602/2025)
coverage.found: Employers fined OMR 10/month for late renewal or registration (individual employers OMR 15, corporate OMR 20), capped at OMR 500 per worker. Affects households and small firms. Overlaps K04 (household domestic-worker file) and K07 (rejected payroll). See C11.

coverage.category: 33. Tenancy and lease registration (RD 6/89 as amended by RD 12/2025, municipal registration)
coverage.found: Landlords must register leases with the municipality and pay 3% of annual rent; non-registration is fined at three times the fee; RD 12/2025 (dated 7 Jan 2025, in force after 6 months) created governorate rent-dispute committees (details unverified: only secondary sources seen). Pool of individual landlords is large but a municipal portal likely exists. See C03.

coverage.category: 34. Hazardous chemicals permits (Environment Authority Decision 50/2023)
coverage.found: Permits to import, export, use, sell or distribute hazardous chemicals (use permit up to 3 years, import/export up to 1 year), semi-annual reports, SDS, quantity limits, 7-working-day delivery rule, Civil Defence storage/transport licence. Buyer pool (paint, cleaning, pool and agri chemical dealers) is unverified. See C05.

coverage.category: 35. Waste licences (Environment Authority: import/transit Decision 51/2023, export 15/2021, hazardous waste transport fees MD 10/2017)
coverage.found: Import/transit licensees must keep records, file annual reports, log data in the Authority's electronic system and fit vehicle tracking devices (in force 1 May 2024). Domestic hazardous waste transport licence valid 2 years (fees RO 75-400 per MD 10/2017, may be superseded). Small buyer pool; no small-hauler register found. Weak (C06).

coverage.category: 36. Beneficial ownership register for LLCs and SAOCs (MOCIIP)
coverage.found: Companies must keep an internal register of 25%+ owners, update within 5 business days, make it available to the Ministry on 3 days' notice, and appoint an Oman-resident liaison. No annual filing. Sanctions: fines up to OMR 1,000 and suspension of the commercial registration. A 2026 amendment claim (six-month compliance) is unconfirmed. Legal basis conflicts between sources (MD 630/2022 or 424/2023). See C08.

coverage.category: 37. Non-profit associations: AML/CFT supervision (MoSD, Ministerial Decision 36/2023)
coverage.found: Associations and non-profit bodies must keep beneficiary and donor records (name, ID copy, address, date of birth), and cash donations over OMR 100 must go through approved channels. No Omani annual-report format found. Small buyer pool and low willingness to pay. See C07b (listed as C15).

coverage.category: 38. Tourism-classified restaurants, cafes, travel offices and tour guides (same regulation as 29)
coverage.found: Classified restaurants/cafes need a tourism classification certificate (3 years, renewal at least 60 days before expiry, OMR 200); travel offices must insure tourists on all organised trips and use licensed guides. Folded into C01 as an extra buyer group.
